conviction_note: Industry loss-cost and competition read-throughs (Progressive Q3 loss/LAE ratio +3.7 pts YoY, ad spend +18%) and Root's own reliance on reserve releases lean negative, offset by a two-year Carvana extension into a Carvana quarter of +39% units, an unused buyback and a 12-days-to-cover short; the bar is disputed across sources and the short is crowded, so p_up sits at 47 on a 13% absolute move, giving -0.78; findings sum to -0.5, so the two measurements agree in sign and size.
bar: Revenue ~$382.9M and EPS $0.61 (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ROOT/earnings-forecasts, via search snippet; page 403 on fetch); Earnings Whispers EPS $0.66 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/ROOT); Bullstory EPS $0.50 (https://bullstory.io/en/stocks/root/earnings/2026-q3). Sources disagree on EPS, so every finding is capped small. No company guide: the Q2 2026 letter gives no numeric guidance, only 'PIF relatively flat YoY if competitive conditions persist' (https://quartr.com/events/root-root-q2-2026_oj97tQvZ). The comparison quarter is Q3 2025: net loss $5M, including a $17M noncash Carvana warrant expense, and a 102.1% net combined ratio. Q2 2026 actual was EPS $1.49 against a $0.67 estimate, revenue $389M, and the stock fell 16%.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest via Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/root/short-interest?range=6m): 2,075,638 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 12.05 days to cover, 13.4% of shares outstanding (15.49M per the Q2 10-Q). That is up from 1.83M on 2026-09-15. Class B and insider and partner holdings mean the share of free float is materially higher, likely ~18-20% (inference). A crowded short. Baseline skew is +0.5 vol points, essentially balanced ('priced_direction_lean': 'balanced'); put/call OI is 1.3; event-implied move is 16.62%. Run-up is +15.35% over 20 days and +5.7% over 5 days into the print, with the stock 39% below its 52-week high. Prior 7 reactions: -16.2, +3.4, -5.5, -8.8, -26.4, +1.1, +25.6 (median abs 8.8). The Q2 2026 EPS beat (1.49 vs 0.67) sold off 16%.

findings.finding: Progressive's Q3 2026 10-Q shows consolidated losses and LAE of $14,904M on $21,869M net premiums earned, a ~68.2% loss/LAE ratio against ~64.5% in Q3 2025 (+3.7 pts YoY), so industry auto loss costs worsened in Q3 while rates were being cut. Root now retains almost all of its risk: ceded premiums written were $2.3M in Q2 2026 against $12.2M a year earlier. Root's own Q2 gross accident-period loss ratio was already 61.6% against 57.4% a year earlier. Consensus EPS of ~$0.61 against Q2's $1.49 already embeds a seasonal step-down; the question is whether it embeds a +3-4 pt YoY trend on top of Q3 2025's ~59.5% gross loss ratio.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loss-ratio-driven prints: Q2 2025 (2025-08-06) fell 26.4% and Q3 2025 fell 8.8%, the latter on margin pressure (StockStory Q3 2025 deep dive headline). Q2 2026 fell 16.2% despite a flat 66% net loss/LAE ratio.
findings.why_not_priced: Root has rallied 15% in 20 days into the print. If the market expected a YoY deterioration in Root's accident-period loss ratio, a stock 39% off its high with a crowded short would be drifting lower into the print rather than running up, and preview estimates would have been cut since August (the latest dated broker action found is a Wells Fargo $61 Hold from September).
findings.independence: This is an industry proxy, not Root's own number. Root's own Q2 2026 letter shows the gross accident-period loss ratio up 4.2 pts YoY (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788882/000178888226000060/q22026shareholderletter.htm). The Q2 10-Q attributes loss costs to higher severity from repair and medical costs.

findings.finding: Root's reported loss ratio is being supported by reserve releases. H1 2026 favorable prior-year development was $28.5M against $14.0M in H1 2025 (Q2 10-Q), and Q2's gross loss ratio of 58.7% sat ~2.9 pts below the 61.6% gross accident-period ratio. If Q3 releases shrink, the reported loss ratio rises even with a stable underlying trend. If they persist, the beat is low-quality, which this stock sold in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EPS of $1.49 against $0.67 consensus, flattered by PYD and a 26.1% expense ratio; the stock fell 16.2% (baseline 2026-08-05; https://stockunlock.com/investing/root-stock-q2-2026-earnings/).
findings.why_not_priced: Previews and aggregators quote the net combined ratio and EPS, not the accident-period ratio or the PYD split. If this were priced, the post-Q2 sell-off would have bottomed and the stock would not have re-rated +15% in 20 days ahead of the next print.
findings.independence: Same company filing family as finding 1's corroboration (the Q2 letter), but a different fact: reserve releases rather than the current-year trend. The PGR 10-Q also shows heavy industry reliance on PYD ($1,536M favorable over 9M per https://beancount.io/blog/2026/10/26/progressive-fy2026-q3-earnings-analysis).

findings.finding: The Q3 2026 competitive environment for Root's direct channel worsened. Progressive's Q3 advertising rose 18% to $1.6B, its average written premium per personal auto policy fell 2% YoY, and its policy life expectancy fell 9% YoY (more churn). GEICO also resumed heavy advertising. Root guided PIF to 'relatively flat YoY if competitive conditions persist' after PIF fell sequentially from 495,429 to 483,921 in Q2, and Q2 GWP was down 2% YoY. So a further sequential PIF and GWP decline and lower retention are the risk, mostly inside what was guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the flat-PIF guide and the sequential PIF decline were the main reason for the -16.2% reaction (StockStory/StockUnlock). Q1 2026's growth-muted warning still produced +3.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely guided, hence the small size. What is not visible is the effect on Root's retention: PGR's 9% drop in policy life expectancy is a churn signal for the whole market, and Root's renewal book is exposed to it. The stock's +15% run-up suggests no one is positioned for a PIF decline beyond flat.
findings.independence: PGR 10-Q Q3 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000379/pgr-20260930.htm). LexisNexis Q2 2026 Demand Meter shows shopping growth slowing to 1.4% YoY (https://risk.lexisnexis.com/about-us/press-room/press-release/20260817-q3-demand-meter). These are proxies, not Root's numbers.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-31 Root and Carvana restructured their partnership: the commercial agreement runs two years to ~2028-08-31 with auto-renewal, exclusivity was rewritten, and deep-OTM 2021 warrants ($180-540 strikes) were swapped for a 1,525,560-share performance warrant. The new warrant has five tranches struck at 130-170% of a $55.72 VWAP and vests at 180k/210k/250k/290k/340k cumulative policies attributed after 2026-08-31. Carvana's Q3 2026 retail units were 217,385, +39% YoY (released 2026-10-28). Partnerships plus agents were ~51% of Root's new writings in Q2, and Carvana had passed 200k lifetime policies by Q1 2026. The milestone ladder implies both sides expect a materially faster attributed-policy run-rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Partnership-channel strength was the stated bright spot of Q1 and Q2 2026, but it did not prevent the -16.2% Q2 reaction, so the stock has not paid for this line on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K was a quiet Item 1.01/3.02 filing with no press release found, and the milestone numbers sit in an exhibit. Carvana's +39% unit growth printed on 2026-10-28, after Root last spoke. If priced, previews would cite the Carvana extension, and none found do. Net of the rest of the company: the direct channel (~49% of new writings) faces finding 3, so this is sized as a partial offset.
findings.independence: Carvana Q3 2026 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001690820/000169082026000066/ex99_1q32026.htm), a different issuer and document. Root Q1 2026 call: 'Carvana surpassed 200,000 policies sold' (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/root-q1-earnings-call-highlights-2026-05-06/).

findings.finding: Carvana warrant accounting is an unquantified one-off in Q3 2026. Q3 2025's $5M GAAP net loss included a $17M noncash Carvana warrant expense, so the YoY GAAP comparison is flattered. The 2026-08-31 cancellation and reissue may create a modification charge or contra-revenue in Q3 2026 whose size the filing does not state.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 printed a GAAP loss on the $17M warrant expense and fell 8.8%, but the reaction was attributed to margin and outlook, not the warrant.
findings.why_not_priced: Estimates disagree across sources ($0.50 / $0.61 / $0.66), which is consistent with analysts treating GAAP items differently. A noncash, below-operating-line item with no path to guidance, sized at zero with a symmetric band.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 CFO remarks on the $17M warrant expense (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2025/11/06/root-root-q3-2025-earnings-call-transcript); shares the Carvana 8-K with finding 4.

findings.finding: Expense ratio normalization was guided. The CFO said Q2's 26.1% net expense ratio is not the new normal, pointed to ~29% (Q1/Q4) as the reference, and expects SBC back at $8-9M a quarter; $10M is allocated to new acquisition channels in H2 2026. Expect Q3 operating income to compress against Q2 on expenses alone, inside what was guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This was guided in Q2 and contributed to that -16.2%. Since it is already told, a match should be near zero.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; filed because it bears on the quarter. Consensus at ~$0.61 against Q2's $1.49 already reflects it.
findings.independence: Quartr Q2 2026 summary on the $10M H2 acquisition channels (https://quartr.com/events/root-root-q2-2026_oj97tQvZ).

findings.finding: Root had ~$54.2M left on its $75M buyback at 2026-06-30, after $20.8M repurchased in H1, and the stock traded ~$48-54 through Q3: Form 4 tax-withholding prices of $53.60 on 2026-09-15 and $49.78 on 2026-09-21, against a $55.72 VWAP on 2026-08-31. Cash was $509.6M against a market cap of ~$850M. Q3 repurchases at those prices and a possible increased authorization land on the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The first buyback disclosure, with Q1 results on 2026-05-06, coincided with +3.4%. The >$20M Q2 repurchase did not offset the Q2 sell-off.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 repurchase volume is not public until the release. Covenants on the new term loan start with the Q3 2026 quarter and require a cash minimum of 25% of principal, which does not constrain a ~$50M buyback against $510M cash.
findings.independence: Form 4s (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1788882/000162828026062547/wk-form4_1789677995.xml) give Q3 share prices only. There is no independent confirmation that buybacks occurred.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 13% in September to 2.08M shares (2026-10-15 settlement), at 12.05 days to cover on ~157k average daily volume. That is ~13.4% of shares outstanding and a larger share of free float. A crowded short on a thin tape, so an in-line or better print with a stable loss ratio has a squeeze mechanism. This partly explains the +15% 20-day run-up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-02-26: +25.6% on a profitability milestone with a heavy short. Shorts were rewarded on the 2025-08-06 (-26.4%) and 2026-08-05 (-16.2%) prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the market's own bet, so this is the reaction function, not a fact. Filed small because 12 days to cover makes the payoff asymmetric for an in-line print, while the +15% run-up suggests some covering already happened.
findings.independence: None from a different source. Benzinga's short-interest page is stale.

findings.finding: Root's next-generation pricing model is due to roll out state by state from late Q4 2026, and New Jersey went live 2026-07-22 (37 states, >80% of the US population, contiguous US targeted by 2027). The Q3 call is the first update on both. A confirmed launch or early NJ volume could support the 2027 growth narrative after the flat-PIF guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 pricing-model announcement with a '2027 impact' did not prevent -16.2%. Product and state-expansion news has not moved this stock on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and announced, so mostly priced. Filed small because the call is the first read on NJ traction and on any slippage of the Q4 pricing-model timing, which no preview carries.
findings.independence: Quartr Q2 2026 summary on the Q4 2026 pricing model launch (https://quartr.com/events/root-root-q2-2026_oj97tQvZ).

outside_window.finding: The Carvana warrant tranches can only vest once 180k+ cumulative attributed policies are reported, quarterly within 15 days of quarter end, over a two-year term. The value of the partnership extension resolves over 2027-2028, not on this print.
